title: Equations of motion (গতির সমীকরণ)
placement: Book pages 45–46, topic 2.7: গতির সমীকরণ (Equations of Motion). Next to the section text on uniform acceleration (v = u + at), in place of a printed picture.
description: The equations of motion (গতির সমীকরণ, pages 45–46, 2.7) laid out in one frame exactly as the owner's reference "Uniform Acceleration in One Dimension", on a soft light-blue background: at the top the formula x = x₀ + ut + ½at² with one short sentence under it (the sum of the three parts, the moment the car turns back, or that it reached an end of the axis); on the left the buttons চালাও (Run), থামাও (Pause), আবার শুরু (Reset) and the two 0.1 s time steps; in the middle four long sliders for the আদি অবস্থান x₀ (red, −5…5 m), the আদি বেগ u (blue, −5…5 m/s; the book's symbol for the reference's v₀), the ত্বরণ a (green, −3…3 ms⁻²) and the সময় t (grey, 0…6 s), steps of 0.1, each value written over its knob in its colour; on the right the x–t graph (a parabola) and the v–t graph (a straight line), growing as t runs with the moment marked, each with its live equation under it, x = (½a)t² + (u)t + (x₀) and v = (a)t + (u); and along the bottom, across the full width, a 3D strip seen from the side: a blue sedan (wheels that turn with the motion) on a dark asphalt road whose front slope carries the number line from −7 m to 10 m (bold numbers every metre), a dot at the car's position x, and under the axis the three parts drawn tip to tail as thick outlined arrows (x₀ red from 0, ut blue, ½at² green ending at x) with a dashed drop line from the car, so x is their sum. চালাও runs the time in real seconds; the car stops at an end of the axis. Portrait frames stack the same parts. Test (in the place of the sliders, from a small tab in the corner): 5 tap questions (x after t with x₀ read off the axis, v = u + at, a read from the x equation, when v = 0 from the v equation, the part ½at² read off the picture), wrong choices from real mistakes, each worked answer naming the mistake and running the car to that moment. Phone-first, Bangla. GLB: the road with its number line and the three arrows, and the car, in metres.
